$comment: nodes=modules, edges=[cause,effect] where cause is imported-by effect. ADD invariants by hand.

revenue-aggregates-in-sql.rule: Revenue and count totals are computed over the full filtered set in the database (SQL aggregate), never summed in JS from a paginated page of rows.
revenue-aggregates-in-sql.why: The classic dashboard lie: page 1 of 20 sums to a number that looks real and is wrong. Ops makes money decisions on this figure.
revenue-aggregates-in-sql.check: grep -rn 'reduce(' frontend/app backend/src | grep -iE 'revenue|total|amount' # must return nothing

ui-never-imports-prisma.rule: No file under frontend/app/** imports @prisma/client directly; all data access goes through the query layer built in M2.
ui-never-imports-prisma.why: Keeps the DB a detail behind one seam, so schema changes hit one module instead of every page. Dependency direction stays inward.
ui-never-imports-prisma.check: grep -rn '@prisma/client' frontend/app | grep -v node_modules # must return nothing

every-db-call-has-a-timeout.rule: Every query to Supabase runs under an explicit timeout and a bounded connection pool. No unbounded await.
every-db-call-has-a-timeout.why: Supabase is reached over the public internet, not a private network. A hung socket with no timeout freezes an ops screen indefinitely during an incident, exactly when it's needed.

dispatch-is-idempotent.rule: Assigning a mechanic to a booking twice results in exactly one assignment and one audit row. Enforced by a DB unique constraint, not by app-level checking.
dispatch-is-idempotent.why: Double-clicked buttons and retried requests are normal. Two mechanics dispatched to one job is a real-world cost, and app-level guards race.
dispatch-is-idempotent.check: cd backend && node --test src/dispatch/ # includes an explicit double-dispatch case
